title: European consumers report growing confidence in their own food choices while trust in the surrounding information environment remains fragile
source_unit: EIT Food Consumer Observatory, Trust Report 2026: Who do consumers believe?
geography: Consumers across 18 European countries; nearly 20,000 respondents in the TrustTracker study

denominator.unit: approximately European consumers surveyed across 18 countries in TrustTracker; exact sample varies by analysis

healthy_diet_knowledge.value: Around 72% felt their knowledge of the healthiness of food was sufficient in 2025, according to the report summary

choice_confidence_information_trust.value: Confidence in personal choices rose while fewer than half considered food information itself reliable

observations.method: EIT Food TrustTracker cross-national consumer research reported in the fourth 2026 Trust Report chapter; repeated survey comparison across 2024 and 2025.
observations.uncertainty: The report page provides headline findings rather than a full public table of question wording, weights, country samples, or uncertainty intervals; confidence is self-reported and does not establish diet quality or realized sustainability.
observations.subgroup: European consumers across 18 countries, with differences potentially shaped by country, age, income, education, diet, and food-system experience.
observations.counterinterpretation: Growing confidence can reflect improved self-efficacy or decision heuristics even when information quality is contested; it does not necessarily mean consumers are misinformed or making worse choices.

denominator.unit: approximately European consumers across 18 countries; multiple source and confidence responses

food_information_reliability.value: Fewer than half considered food information reliable

trusted_source_discovery.unit: percent saying they know where to find sources they can trust

self_assessed_discrimination.value: Consumers reported growing confidence in separating reliable from unreliable information

information_gap.value: Personal confidence and source-environment confidence moved in different directions

observations.method: Cross-national TrustTracker measures of perceived information reliability, source discovery, and self-assessed ability to distinguish reliable information.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not provide an objective accuracy test, source-specific causal attribution, or a behavioral measure of whether respondents actually use trusted sources.
observations.subgroup: Consumers using food labels, health and sustainability information, media, expert sources, retailers, manufacturers, public authorities, and informal networks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Knowing where to find trusted sources may be a meaningful information capability even if trust in the broader information environment remains low.

denominator.unit: EIT Food report recommendations derived from the 18-country consumer study

needed_information.value: Accessible, understandable, clearly sourced, transparent, third-party validated, concise, evidence-based information

trust_problem.value: Consumers need information they can understand, assess, and trust rather than simply more information

stakeholder_route.value: The report addresses policymakers, researchers, food businesses, and communicators

observations.method: Synthesis and recommendations from a consumer-observatory report series linking trust, knowledge, and behavior.
observations.uncertainty: Recommendations are not an evaluated intervention; the study cannot show which communication or validation mechanism changes purchasing, diet, health, or sustainability outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Food consumers, businesses, public authorities, researchers, educators, communicators, and third-party validators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Information design may improve usability without resolving affordability, habit, time, access, or cultural meaning constraints that shape food choices.

denominator.unit: approximately consumers surveyed across 18 European countries in the Trust Report series

series_scope.value: The 2026 series covers intention and diet, food-system trust, innovation trust, and who consumers believe

behavior_link.value: The series frames trust, knowledge, and behavior as interacting influences on food choices

innovation_context.value: Food-technology openness is treated as connected to familiarity and cultural perceptions

observations.method: Consumer-observatory series using repeated cross-national survey evidence and thematic chapters.
observations.uncertainty: The conceptual relationship among trust, knowledge, and behavior is not a causal model; chapter-level measures may differ in samples, timing, and operational definitions.
observations.subgroup: Consumers facing health, affordability, sustainability, innovation, and cultural-choice tradeoffs in European food systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Trust can be a condition for adoption but not a substitute for price, availability, taste, convenience, household time, or institutional regulation.

related_sources.claim: EIT Food report library and chapter context.
Related food-system trust chapter covering trust in farmers, retailers, manufacturers, restaurants, and authorities.

boundary: This record adds a European food-information and consumer-trust layer. It uses self-reported, cross-national TrustTracker survey findings summarized on the EIT Food report page; it does not provide a public respondent-level file, objective accuracy test, causal model, realized diet or sustainability outcomes, or intervention evaluation. The report is produced by an agrifood consumer-observatory organization and should be read with its sponsorship and disclosure context.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: EIT Food report page reviewed for publication date, 18-country scope, approximately 20,000 respondents, confidence change, information reliability, trusted-source discovery, and recommendations.
